metadata.releaseNotes:
A fresh new Univest, built for a faster experience

What's new:

A. A brand new app header look for a faster - focussed access
B. Reimagined Market's experience - easier to scan, easier to act on
C. New Sector Performance widget - track which sectors are heating up or cooling off
D. Smoother trial activation - Activating your free trial is now faster and clearer

Bundled with a lot of bug fixes and minor experience improvements
metadata.description:
Trusted by 50 lakh+ investors | SEBI-Registered Advisory

Looking for a stock market advisory app that gives you real, research-backed trade ideas? Univest is India's fastest-growing investment app, combining AI stock recommendations with expert analysis from SEBI-registered research analysts.

Whether you trade in stocks, F&O, or equity, Univest delivers personalized Buy, Sell, and Hold signals directly to your phone. No guesswork. No noise. Just clear, actionable trade ideas backed by data and professional research.

WHAT MAKES UNIVEST DIFFERENT

Unlike other trading apps, Univest is not a broker. It is a pure advisory platform. You get the recommendations, you stay in full control of your trades. Every recommendation comes from SEBI-registered analysts with transparent track records.

KEY FEATURES

Stock Market Advisory
Get daily trade ideas for intraday, short-term, and positional trading. Each recommendation includes entry price, target, and stop-loss. Backed by research from SEBI

reviews.author: SamantaSoumen
reviews.title: Targets Rarely Achieved, Losses Hidden
reviews.content:
I am extremely disappointed with Univest. The app promotes short-term, mid-term, and long-term stock recommendations with specific targets and holding periods, but the reality is very different after purchasing the subscription.

Many trades are closed much earlier than the stated target period, sometimes on the same day or within a few days, with just 1–2% profit. The advertised target is rarely achieved because profits are booked prematurely. 

On the other hand, when a trade goes into loss, it is often left open for months or even hundreds of days. In some cases, additional buying is recommended, and eventually the trade is closed after 300–600 days with only 2–3% profit.

Another major issue is the lack of transparency. Winning trades are highlighted, but running loss-making trades are not properly showcased. This creates a misleading impression of overall performance and makes it difficult for subscribers to assess the actual success rate.

The app also constantly pushes Futures &

reviews.author: Navitewatia22
reviews.title: Fake site hai, logo ka bewkuf bana kr paisa loot rhe hai
reviews.content: You're warning that *"Univest App" is a fake app* run by highly educated, very clever people who trap investors. *How they trap people:* 1. I have been connected with the app for 2 years 2. I took 3-4 trades on their advice - *all were losses* 3. Their method: They pick stocks that have _already risen_ 4-7% in a day/week 4. They then tell users to "buy now for 4-5% potential" 5. Example: Stock goes from ₹500 to ₹550, they give entry at ₹550 6. If you're lucky, it goes up 2-4% more and they make you exit for a tiny profit 7. But usually, you buy at the high and *it falls immediately* - then you're trapped for years 8. I am personally stuck in 3 of their stocks for 3 years now 9. They either move it to "long term/medium term" or make you exit at 1-1.5% instead of 5% 10. You can't track it all day, so you don't realize they're exiting early *My advice*: It's totally fraud, fake membership, fake people. Don't Invest.

reviews.author: Mohanhnkumar
reviews.title: Trade Calls After the Move Has Already Happened
reviews.content:
By the time they post a trade on the app, the opportunity is often already gone and the stock has moved out of the ideal buying range. Yet, they continue to highlight the profits made on those trades.
It feels as though, instead of sharing actionable trades that users can enter, they are posting trades that would have been useful a few minutes earlier.
I followed several of their trade calls closely and noticed that the entry prices, exit prices, and profit figures they publish often do not align with the actual timing of their posts.
